1.House of the Blackheads
A lavishly restored Gothic-Renaissance merchant guild house from 1334, demolished by the Soviets and rebuilt stone by stone in the 1990s — the most photographed building in all of Latvia.

2.Latvian Occupation Museum
A sober and essential museum documenting Latvia's twin occupations under Soviet and Nazi rule from 1940 to 1991, with thousands of testimonies, personal artefacts and photographs housed in a striking concrete pavilion in the heart of Old Town.

3.Bastejkalns Park
A tranquil hillside park tracing Riga's historic city moat, with red-brick bastion terraces, weeping willows, a stone-arched bridge and swan-filled canal waters at the western edge of Old Town.

4.Riga Cathedral
Latvia's oldest place of worship and the largest medieval church in the Baltic, containing one of Europe's greatest Baroque pipe organs with 6,768 pipes and a richly layered cloister from the 13th century.

Day 2
From Hotel: 9 min · 3 min → Freedom Monument
1.Freedom Monument
A solemn 42-metre granite and travertine column topped by a bronze Liberty figure, unveiled in 1935, preserved throughout Soviet occupation and guarded by the Latvian Guard of Honour 24 hours a day.
Read more
Open 24/7

2.National Museum of Art
Latvia's leading fine-arts museum, occupying a grand neoclassical palace from 1905, with a collection of 52,000 works spanning centuries of Baltic and European painting from the 18th century to the present.

Set inside a meticulously preserved apartment house from 1903, this museum recreates the lavish living spaces of a prosperous Riga family and brings to life the ornate stucco facades that make the city a UNESCO heritage site.

From Hotel: 15 min → Latvian Ethnographic Museum
1.Latvian Ethnographic Museum
The world's oldest open-air museum and one of Europe's largest, with over 100 historic farmsteads, windmills, a church and a fishermen's village spread across 87 hectares of lakeside forest east of the city.
Read more
Daily 10:00am - 5:00pm

2.Riga Motor Museum
Latvia's most theatrical museum, displaying 130 immaculately restored Soviet and Western vehicles — including Leonid Brezhnev's personal ZIL limousines — inside a dramatic building architecturally shaped like a speeding automobile.

Tuesday - Sunday 10:00am - 5:00pm

3.Riga Zoo
Founded in 1912 and one of the Baltic's oldest zoos, home to over 3,000 animals including rare white lions, Amur tigers and Przewalski's horses in a beautifully forested park-like setting adjacent to Mežaparks.

A lush century-old forest park on the shores of Ķīšezers lake, designed in 1901 as a garden suburb, with open-air concert grounds, cycle paths and shaded lakeside promenades popular with Riga locals all year round.

Local Tastes
Pelēkie zirņi ar speķi
Latvia's most beloved comfort dish: slow-cooked grey peas with thick-cut smoked pork belly and caramelised onion, traditionally served at Midsummer and winter celebrations.
Folkklubs Ala Pagrabs · Peldu iela 19 · Old Town
Rupjmaize
Latvia's defining bread — dense, sour and baked with caraway seeds; pick up a loaf at any local bakery or deli and eat it with butter, smoked fish and a sliced onion the traditional Latvian way.
Riga Central Market · Nēģu iela 7 · Old Town
Sklandrausis
A thin open rye-pastry boat filled with sweetened carrot and potato, dusted with caraway — an ancient Latvian pie under EU protected-origin status, best eaten fresh from a traditional restaurant.
Rozengrāls · Rozena iela 1 · Old Town
Auksti kūpinātas zivis
Cold-smoked Baltic sprats and pike-perch — a cornerstone of the Latvian diet, sold at market stalls and specialist fishmongers; eat with dark rye bread, butter and a sliced onion.
Riga Central Market · Nēģu iela 7 · Old Town
Rīgas Melnais Balzams
A 45% herbal liqueur made to a secret 24-ingredient recipe since 1752, served as a digestif or mixed into black currant juice — Latvia's unofficial national drink, available at any bar in the city.
Any Old Town bar · Riga Old Town

Worth Knowing

Riga's Old Town fits in an hour — but the Art Nouveau district takes all morning

Riga has one of the world's highest concentrations of Art Nouveau architecture; the blocks around Alberta, Elizabetes and Strēlnieku streets are best explored before 10am when tour groups arrive. Pick up a free Art Nouveau guide at the tourist information office on Rātslaukums.

The euro is the currency; ATMs are everywhere in the centre. Most city-centre restaurants, cafés and museums accept cards, though smaller market vendors and kiosks may prefer cash.

English is widely spoken by anyone working in tourism, hotels and restaurants. Outside those contexts Latvian and Russian are the languages you'll hear; signs in Old Town are also in English.

The Riga Card covers unlimited public transport and free or reduced entry to 25 museums including the Motor Museum and the Ethnographic Open-Air Museum — good value if visiting both on Day 3.

Amber sold in Old Town is genuine Baltic amber, but quality and price vary widely. Look for vendors displaying the Latvian Amber Association certification mark; avoid the cheapest stalls near Rātslaukums, which may sell pressed amber.
